findings.title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before the new code that enables Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES. upgradeStrategy() yields null as well as RECREATE, and both testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount deploy that CR. The operator guide added in this change says that while the feature is preview, rolling-updates must be enabled or the Operator fails, and the CR example enables it even when strategy is left unset. The null cases therefore never put rolling-updates on spec.features.enabled. deployKeycloak(..., true) will time out if reconciliation fails closed without the feature. If the operator instead shells out to update-compatibility, that command now exits 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED) before it can report compatibility, so testCacheMaxCount(null) cannot observe the rolling update it asserts. Enable the feature for every strategy before that return. On the explicit-strategy path, setEnabledFeatures(List.of(rolling-updates)) also replaces any enabled-feature list already on the spec instead of adding rolling-updates, so other features configured by the test deployment would be dropped.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is documented as a rolling-upgrade incompatibility
findings.body: The check-command exit-code table says exit code 4 means "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" because rolling-updates is disabled. That is not what the implementation does. Both update-compatibility check and update-compatibility metadata return CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4) before any version or config comparison, after printing "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." The deployment may still be rolling-compatible; the tool refused to run. Exit code 3 uses the same "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" headline and tells the operator to shut the deployment down first. Scripts that follow this table and treat 4 like 3 will take unnecessary downtime, and a metadata-generation step that exits 4 will be misread as an upgrade incompatibility. Document 4 as a precondition failure for both subcommands: enable rolling-updates and re-run; do not shut down the cluster.

findings.title: Remapped compatibility exit codes are not asserted
findings.body: This change moves the recreate result from exit code 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to FEATURE_DISABLED, and the guide tells automation to rely on those codes rather than log text. testFeatureNotEnabled only checks that stderr contains the feature-disabled sentence; it never asserts exit code 4, and it only launches the metadata subcommand, not check, which has the same gate. testWrongVersions asserts the incompatibility text but not exit code 3, and the check invocation in testCompatible does not assert exit code 0. A regression that still prints the expected line but exits 4 for an incompatible version (the previous recreate code) or exits 1 after the feature-disabled message would pass CI and break scripts that branch on the exit code.
